Use AI in as many processes as possible across the organization this year
Reduce average claims processing time from 10 days to 6 days by year end

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Good key results are specific, measurable, and time-bound, with a baseline and target.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Become the most innovative company in the…: Aspirational and not measurable.
• Launch several exciting AI pilots that…: Vague and measures sentiment, not outcomes.
• Use AI in as many processes as possible…: Vague and not tied to an outcome.

Key takeaway: Key results should be specific, measurable, and time-bound.

stem: A company rolled out an AI coding assistant and developer output rose, but defects in production also rose. What does this suggest about value measurement?

choices.text: Productivity gains must be weighed against quality costs, so defect rates belong in the KPIs
Defects are unrelated to development tools, so the increase must have a completely different cause
The assistant should be removed immediately, since any increase in defects cancels all benefits
Developer output is the only metric that matters, so the defect increase can be ignored safely

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Higher output with more defects may reduce net value. Including quality metrics shows the full picture and guides controls such as review practices.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Defects are unrelated to development tools,…: The timing suggests a link that should be examined.
• The assistant should be removed immediately,…: The tool may still be net positive with better review practices.
• Developer output is the only metric that…: Ignoring defects overstates value.

Key takeaway: Pair productivity metrics with quality metrics.

stem: A company wants to differentiate its customer service with AI. Which approach is least likely to be copied by competitors?

choices.text: Train staff and AI together on the company's unique service processes and customer history
Announce the chatbot with a larger advertising campaign than any competitor can afford
Use a public foundation model with a generic prompt that any company could write easily
License the same off-the-shelf chatbot product that competitors are already using

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Combining unique processes, proprietary history, and trained people creates an experience that is hard to replicate.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Announce the chatbot with a larger…: Advertising can be matched and does not improve service.
• Use a public foundation model with a generic…: Generic prompts are easy to copy.
• License the same off-the-shelf chatbot…: Identical products give no differentiation.

Key takeaway: Differentiate with proprietary processes and data, not common tools.

stem: A company must decide whether a use case even needs AI. Which TWO signals suggest AI is a good fit? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The company has no data related to the task and no way of collecting any in the future
Every output must be exactly reproducible and follow a published formula without any exception at all
The task involves patterns in large volumes of data that are hard to capture with explicit rules
The task happens once a year and takes a single employee about ten minutes to complete
Some errors are tolerable and can be caught by review or correction processes

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AI fits when patterns are too complex for rules and when occasional errors can be managed. Exact, rule-defined, data-less, or trivial tasks rarely justify AI.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The company has no data related to the task…: Without data, most AI approaches cannot work.
• Every output must be exactly reproducible…: Exact formula-driven tasks fit deterministic software.
• The task happens once a year and takes a…: The effort far exceeds the benefit.

Key takeaway: Use AI where patterns are complex and errors are manageable.

stem: A company estimates AI value using the vendor's case study from a much larger customer. What is the main risk?

choices.text: Larger customers always see smaller benefits, so this company will see much greater value
Results depend on context, so benefits may not transfer to this company's scale, data, and processes
The only risk is that the vendor may raise prices after the company signs the contract
Case studies are always false, so any vendor-reported results should be assumed to have zero value here

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Value depends on the organization's data, processes, and scale. Estimates should be grounded in the company's own baseline and ideally a pilot.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Larger customers always see smaller…: There is no rule that smaller companies gain more.
• The only risk is that the vendor may raise…: Pricing risk exists but is not the main issue with this estimate.
• Case studies are always false, so any…: Case studies can be informative, just not directly transferable.

Key takeaway: Ground value estimates in your own baselines and pilots.

stem: A company considers joining an industry consortium that shares anonymized data to train fraud models. Which consideration matters most?

choices.text: Whether the consortium's logo will appear on the company's public website after the partnership is formally announced
Whether the consortium meets in person or online, since meeting format decides the value created
Whether competitors also join, since the company should only join groups its competitors avoid
Whether shared learning improves detection enough to outweigh losing some exclusivity of the company's data

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Consortium data can improve models for everyone, but it reduces how unique the company's data advantage is. The decision weighs that trade-off, along with privacy terms.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Whether the consortium's logo will appear on…: Logo placement is marketing.
• Whether the consortium meets in person or…: Meeting format does not determine value.
• Whether competitors also join, since the…: Competitor participation is often the point of such consortia.

Key takeaway: Weigh shared-data gains against the loss of data exclusivity.

stem: A product team says its churn model outputs 'a probability of 0.82' for a customer. How should account managers interpret this?

choices.text: Exactly 82% of the customer's active contracts will be cancelled, and the remaining 18% will be renewed automatically
The customer will definitely leave within 82 days unless the account manager offers a discount immediately
The model is 82% finished with its training and will produce final answers once training has completed
The model estimates a high likelihood of churn, not a certainty, so it should guide priority rather than decide alone

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Model outputs are often probabilities. A score of 0.82 indicates high estimated risk, which should prioritize action, not replace judgment.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Exactly 82% of the customer's active…: The number is a likelihood for the customer, not a split of contracts.
• The customer will definitely leave within 82…: A probability is not a certainty or a time frame.
• The model is 82% finished with its training…: The score is a prediction, not training progress.

Key takeaway: Treat model scores as probabilities that guide decisions, not certainties.

stem: A data science lead explains that the team holds back part of the data that the model never sees during training. Why?

choices.text: To test the model on unseen data and estimate how it will perform on real future cases
To keep sensitive records out of the model, since held-back data is automatically encrypted
To save storage costs, since keeping all of the data in training would require a larger bucket
To reduce the time needed for training, since smaller datasets are always more accurate

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A held-out test set estimates how the model generalizes to new data, which is what matters in production.

Why the other options are wrong:
• To keep sensitive records out of the model,…: Holding data back does not encrypt it.
• To save storage costs, since keeping all of…: Storage cost is not the reason.
• To reduce the time needed for training,…: Smaller training sets are not always more accurate.

Key takeaway: Evaluate models on data they did not train on.

stem: A bank wants to automatically read handwritten and typed fields from loan application forms and verify them against its records. Which combination of AI capabilities fits?

choices.text: A recommendation model that suggests which loan product each applicant would most likely want to buy
Document extraction to read the fields, followed by rule-based checks against existing records
Speech recognition to capture each applicant reading the form aloud during a phone call
Image generation to recreate each form digitally, followed by manual retyping of every field

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Extraction turns documents into data, and deterministic checks verify that data against records, combining AI with rules where each fits best.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A recommendation model that suggests which…: Recommendations do not read or verify forms.
• Speech recognition to capture each applicant…: Speech is not the input.
• Image generation to recreate each form…: Generated images do not extract data.

Key takeaway: Combine AI extraction with rule-based verification.

stem: A streaming service wants to recommend shows and also explain to users why each show was suggested. Which approach best meets both needs?

choices.text: A translation model that converts the show catalog into the user's preferred language before suggesting
A random selection of popular shows, since users cannot tell how recommendations are chosen anyway
A recommendation model whose outputs are paired with explanations based on the user's viewing history
A text generation model that invents a reason for each suggestion without looking at viewing history

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Recommendations grounded in behavior, with explanations tied to that behavior, are both relevant and understandable to users.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A translation model that converts the show…: Translation does not recommend or explain.
• A random selection of popular shows, since…: Random picks are not personalized.
• A text generation model that invents a…: Invented reasons are misleading.

Key takeaway: Pair recommendations with explanations grounded in real signals.

stem: A manager reads that a model's output is limited to '1,000 tokens.' What is a token?

choices.text: A small unit of text, such as a word or part of a word, used to measure model input and output
A prepaid payment voucher that the company must buy in advance before using any foundation model
A single complete document, so the model can return at most 1,000 documents per request
A security credential that proves a user is allowed to call the model's API endpoint

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Tokens are chunks of text that models read and write; limits and pricing are usually expressed in tokens.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A prepaid payment voucher that the company…: Tokens are units of text, not vouchers.
• A single complete document, so the model can…: A token is far smaller than a document.
• A security credential that proves a user is…: That describes an authentication token, not a text token.

Key takeaway: Tokens are units of text that drive limits and cost.

stem: A company's assistant needs to use today's exchange rates, which change daily, in its answers. Which approach is most reliable?

choices.text: Include last year's exchange rates in the system prompt, since rates change only slightly over time
Have the assistant call a rates service at question time and use the returned values in its answer
Ask the model to estimate current rates from its training data, since models know recent market data
Fine-tune the model every day on the latest exchange rates so it memorizes the current values

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Live, frequently changing data should be fetched when needed, through a tool or API call, rather than relying on model memory or training.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Include last year's exchange rates in the…: Old rates can be materially wrong.
• Ask the model to estimate current rates from…: Training data is dated and cannot know today's rates.
• Fine-tune the model every day on the latest…: Daily fine-tuning is costly and still lags.

Key takeaway: Fetch live data through tools; do not rely on model memory.

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a multimodal model from a text-only model?

choices.text: A multimodal model supports several languages, while a text-only model supports only English text
A multimodal model can run in several AWS Regions, while a text-only model runs in one Region only
A multimodal model is always cheaper to use than a text-only model, regardless of the task at hand
A multimodal model can take in and reason over more than one kind of input, such as images and text

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Multimodal models handle multiple input types, such as images plus text, enabling tasks like answering questions about a photo.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A multimodal model supports several…: Language support is a different property.
• A multimodal model can run in several AWS…: Regional availability is unrelated.
• A multimodal model is always cheaper to use…: Cost depends on model and usage.

Key takeaway: Multimodal = multiple input types, such as text and images.

stem: A company trained a model on data from 2020 to 2022. It is used in 2026 and performs worse each month. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: Models always lose exactly one percent of accuracy per month regardless of changes in the data
The model's software license expired in 2023, which gradually reduces its accuracy each month
Customer behavior and conditions changed since training, so the model's learned patterns are outdated
The model is too accurate for 2026 data, so it needs to be made less precise to fit the current business needs

explanation:
Why this is correct:
When the world changes, the data a model sees drifts from what it learned. Monitoring and retraining on recent data address this.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Models always lose exactly one percent of…: There is no fixed decay rate.
• The model's software license expired in…: Licenses do not change model accuracy.
• The model is too accurate for 2026 data, so…: Being too accurate is not the problem.

Key takeaway: Models age as the world changes; monitor and retrain.

stem: A retailer wants shoppers to search for products by uploading a photo of an item they like. Which AI capability enables this?

choices.text: Speech recognition that converts a shopper's spoken product description into text
Sentiment analysis of product reviews to find the items shoppers like the most overall
Visual similarity search that matches the uploaded image to catalog product images
Forecasting that predicts which products will sell best during the next season

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Image-based search compares visual features of the uploaded photo with catalog images to find similar items.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Speech recognition that converts a shopper's…: Speech is not the input.
• Sentiment analysis of product reviews to…: Sentiment ranks reviews, not visual similarity.
• Forecasting that predicts which products…: Forecasting predicts demand, not matches.

Key takeaway: Image-based product search relies on visual similarity.

stem: A company's generative AI assistant sometimes gives different answers to the same policy question. Which TWO changes improve consistency? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Lower the temperature setting for this use case
Increase the maximum output length for each response
Remove the system prompt so the model has fewer instructions
Switch to a model that has a larger image-generation capability
Ground answers in the same retrieved policy text each time

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Lower temperature reduces randomness, and grounding in the same source text anchors the content of answers.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Increase the maximum output length for each…: Longer outputs do not improve consistency.
• Remove the system prompt so the model has…: Removing instructions tends to increase variation.
• Switch to a model that has a larger…: Image generation is unrelated.

Key takeaway: For consistent answers, reduce randomness and ground in the same sources.

stem: An executive asks how 'AI,' 'machine learning,' and 'deep learning' relate. Which answer is accurate?

choices.text: Deep learning is the broadest category, and AI is a narrow technique used only for image recognition
They are three unrelated technologies that happen to share similar marketing language from vendors
AI and machine learning are identical terms, while deep learning refers to storing data deep in long-term archives
Machine learning is a subset of AI, and deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses neural networks

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AI is the broad field; machine learning learns from data; deep learning is machine learning with multi-layer neural networks.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Deep learning is the broadest category, and…: The hierarchy is reversed.
• They are three unrelated technologies that…: They are nested, not unrelated.
• AI and machine learning are identical terms,…: Deep learning is a learning method, not storage.

Key takeaway: AI ⊃ machine learning ⊃ deep learning.

stem: A hospital wants AI to help radiologists by highlighting possible anomalies in scans. Which design principle is most appropriate?

choices.text: Show radiologists only the scans the AI marks as normal, so they can focus on routine cases
Use AI as decision support that flags findings for radiologists, who make the final diagnosis
Let AI make final diagnoses automatically, since models never tire and are always more accurate
Avoid AI entirely, since any tool that can make mistakes should never be used in healthcare

explanation:
Why this is correct:
In high-stakes domains, AI works best as an assistant that improves human decisions, with experts retaining final responsibility.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Show radiologists only the scans the AI…: Hiding flagged scans defeats the purpose.
• Let AI make final diagnoses automatically,…: Full automation removes necessary oversight and models do make errors.
• Avoid AI entirely, since any tool that can…: Assistive AI can improve outcomes when overseen.

Key takeaway: In high-stakes settings, use AI to support experts, not replace them.

stem: A company wants a model to classify support tickets into categories but has only a handful of labeled examples. Which approach can work quickly?

choices.text: Asking customers to classify their own tickets and removing any automated classification entirely
Waiting until the company collects one million labeled tickets before attempting classification
Few-shot prompting a foundation model with a small number of labeled examples in the prompt
Training a new deep learning model from scratch using only the handful of labeled examples

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Foundation models can perform classification from a few examples in the prompt, which works well when labeled data is scarce.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Asking customers to classify their own…: Self-classification is unreliable and burdens customers.
• Waiting until the company collects one…: Waiting forgoes value unnecessarily.
• Training a new deep learning model from…: A handful of examples is far too few to train from scratch.

Key takeaway: With few labels, try few-shot prompting before training.

stem: Which TWO data practices most improve a model's reliability? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Collecting as many unrelated datasets as possible to increase the data volume
Checking data for errors, duplicates, and missing values before training
Using only the most recent week of data to keep the dataset small and fast
Removing all rare cases so that the model focuses only on common examples
Making sure training data reflects the situations the model will face in use

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Clean, representative data is the foundation of reliable models. Quantity without relevance or quality does not help.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Collecting as many unrelated datasets as…: Unrelated data adds noise.
• Using only the most recent week of data to…: One week is rarely representative.
• Removing all rare cases so that the model…: Rare cases often matter most.

Key takeaway: Quality and representativeness beat sheer volume.

stem: A company plans an AI tool that suggests salaries for new hires based on past offers. What is the main responsible AI concern?

choices.text: Hiring managers may prefer a different font on the page that shows salary suggestions
Salary suggestions will take too long to generate for hiring managers during interviews
The tool may use too much storage because salary records are usually very large files
Past offers may reflect historical pay gaps, which the model could learn and repeat

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Models trained on historical decisions can reproduce historical inequities. Pay data should be checked for gaps and outcomes monitored.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Hiring managers may prefer a different font…: Presentation is cosmetic.
• Salary suggestions will take too long to…: Speed is not the main concern.
• The tool may use too much storage because…: Salary records are small.

Key takeaway: Historical decisions can encode bias that models will learn.

stem: A company's content moderation model can be tuned to catch more harmful posts at the cost of wrongly removing more legitimate posts. How should leadership approach the setting?

choices.text: Choose the balance deliberately based on the harms of each error type, and provide an appeal path
Let the model vendor pick the threshold, since vendors know best what each company's users need
Always maximize removal of harmful content, since wrongly removed posts have no real consequences
Always minimize wrongful removals, since harmful content is the users' own responsibility to avoid

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Both error types cause harm. Leadership should weigh them for the platform's context, set the threshold accordingly, and let people contest mistakes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Let the model vendor pick the threshold,…: The company is accountable for its own policy choices.
• Always maximize removal of harmful content,…: Wrongful removals harm users and trust.
• Always minimize wrongful removals, since…: Ignoring harmful content harms users and the platform.

Key takeaway: Set AI thresholds deliberately by weighing the harms of each error type.

stem: What is the purpose of an 'AI system inventory' in an AI governance program?

choices.text: To list the laptops, servers, and GPUs that the data science team uses for its model development work
To record which AI systems exist, their owners, purposes, and risk levels so they can be overseen
To track the office supplies purchased for the AI center of excellence each quarter
To catalog the AI conferences employees attended during the year for training budgets

explanation:
Why this is correct:
An inventory gives governance visibility: what AI is in use, who owns it, what it does, and how risky it is.

Why the other options are wrong:
• To list the laptops, servers, and GPUs that…: Hardware lists are IT asset management.
• To track the office supplies purchased for…: Supplies are unrelated.
• To catalog the AI conferences employees…: Conference tracking is training administration.

Key takeaway: You cannot govern AI you have not inventoried.

stem: A company buys an AI product from a vendor for use in hiring. Which governance responsibility remains with the company?

choices.text: Only training recruiters on the product's interface, since fairness is purely a technical matter for the vendor
None, since the vendor is fully responsible for any outcomes produced by its AI product
Assessing and monitoring how the product performs and affects candidates in the company's own hiring
Only paying the vendor's invoices on time, since use of the product is the vendor's concern

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Organizations deploying AI remain accountable for its use and effects in their context, even when the product comes from a vendor.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Only training recruiters on the product's…: Fairness in use is the company's responsibility too.
• None, since the vendor is fully responsible…: Accountability for use stays with the deployer.
• Only paying the vendor's invoices on time,…: Payment is not governance.

Key takeaway: Buying AI does not outsource accountability for how it is used.

stem: A company worries that its public-facing chatbot could be used to generate offensive content that is then shared with the company's brand attached. Which control most directly addresses this?

choices.text: Content filters on inputs and outputs that block harmful categories
A larger model, since larger models never produce offensive content
Limiting the chatbot to business hours so fewer people can use it for misuse
A disclaimer at the bottom of the page stating that the company is not responsible

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Filters applied to both prompts and responses block harmful content before it is shown, reducing brand and user harm.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A larger model, since larger models never…: Larger models can still produce harmful content.
• Limiting the chatbot to business hours so…: Hours limits reduce use but not misuse.
• A disclaimer at the bottom of the page…: Disclaimers do not prevent harm.

Key takeaway: Filter harmful content on both inputs and outputs.

stem: A company relies on a single AI vendor for a critical customer process. Which risk-mitigation step is most prudent?

choices.text: Assume the vendor's service will always be available, since large vendors never have outages
Move every other business process to the same vendor to simplify the vendor relationship
Avoid documenting the process so that competitors cannot learn how it works internally
Plan a fallback, such as a manual process or alternate model, and test it periodically

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Critical processes need continuity plans. A tested fallback limits disruption if the AI service is unavailable or degrades.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Assume the vendor's service will always be…: All services can have outages.
• Move every other business process to the…: Concentrating everything increases dependency.
• Avoid documenting the process so that…: Missing documentation makes recovery harder.

Key takeaway: Plan and test fallbacks for critical AI dependencies.

stem: A mental health app uses AI to respond to users. Which safeguard is most important?

choices.text: Collect as much personal data as possible to personalize every response
Hide the fact that responses are AI-generated so users feel more comfortable
Make responses as long as possible so users feel the app is thorough and caring
Detect signs of crisis and route users to human help and emergency resources

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Vulnerable users in crisis need human support. Detecting risk and escalating is essential for safety.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Collect as much personal data as possible to…: Collecting excess data increases privacy risk.
• Hide the fact that responses are…: Hiding AI use undermines trust and informed use.
• Make responses as long as possible so users…: Length does not ensure safety.

Key takeaway: Protect vulnerable users with escalation to human help.

stem: Which TWO practices best prepare a company for regulatory audits of its AI systems? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Rely on employees' memories of how each system was built and tested in the past
Describe AI systems only in marketing materials and avoid internal documentation
Keep documentation of each system's purpose, data, testing, and risk assessments
Delete old model versions and logs promptly to minimize what auditors can request
Retain logs that show how systems behaved and which controls were active

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Audits require evidence: documentation of design and assessments, and logs showing how systems actually operated.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Rely on employees' memories of how each…: Memory is unreliable and not auditable.
• Describe AI systems only in marketing…: Marketing is not evidence.
• Delete old model versions and logs promptly…: Deleting records undermines accountability and may breach obligations.

Key takeaway: Documentation plus operational logs make AI auditable.

stem: Which risk is most specific to AI agents that take actions, compared with assistants that only answer questions?

choices.text: Producing an answer that uses more words than necessary for the user's question
Taking an unintended real-world action, such as issuing a refund or deleting a record
Taking a few seconds longer to respond than a traditional web search would take
Responding in a formal tone when the user expected a more casual conversational tone

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Agents that act on systems can cause real consequences, so action limits, approvals, and logging are critical.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Producing an answer that uses more words…: Verbosity is a minor quality issue.
• Taking a few seconds longer to respond than…: Latency is a performance issue.
• Responding in a formal tone when the user…: Tone is a style issue.

Key takeaway: Agents raise the stakes: errors become actions.

stem: A company publishes responsible AI principles but teams do not apply them. Which step best turns principles into practice?

choices.text: Embed the principles into checklists, review gates, and tools used during development and approval
Ask each employee to sign the principles once a year, without changing any of the development processes
Rewrite the principles in more inspiring language so that employees remember them more easily
Print the principles on posters and display them in every office meeting room and hallway

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Principles become practice when they are built into the processes and tools teams use, such as required reviews and checklists.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Ask each employee to sign the principles…: Annual signatures do not create action.
• Rewrite the principles in more inspiring…: Better wording does not create compliance.
• Print the principles on posters and display…: Posters raise awareness but do not change process.

Key takeaway: Operationalize principles through processes and review gates.

stem: A company wants employees to know which AI tools are approved and how to use them safely. Which artifact serves this best?

choices.text: A spreadsheet of model benchmark scores collected from public leaderboards
A technical architecture document describing the network design of the data center
A press release about the company's AI investments sent to financial journalists
An acceptable use policy that lists approved tools, allowed data, and prohibited uses

explanation:
Why this is correct:
An acceptable use policy tells employees clearly what they may use, with which data, and what is prohibited.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A spreadsheet of model benchmark scores…: Benchmarks do not guide safe use.
• A technical architecture document describing…: Architecture documents serve engineers.
• A press release about the company's AI…: Press releases are external communication.

Key takeaway: Give employees a clear acceptable use policy for AI.

stem: A company can deploy an AI feature now with basic safeguards or wait three months to add stronger testing. The feature affects customer credit limits. Which choice is most responsible?

choices.text: Launch without safeguards, since customers can always call support if a credit limit is wrong
Complete stronger testing first, or launch in a limited, closely monitored way with human review
Cancel the feature permanently, since any use of AI in credit decisions is unacceptable to all regulators
Launch to all customers immediately, since competitors may release similar features soon

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Credit decisions significantly affect customers. Stronger testing, or a limited launch with human review, reduces the risk of harm while still progressing.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Launch without safeguards, since customers…: Relying on complaints shifts harm onto customers.
• Cancel the feature permanently, since any…: Well-governed AI can be used in credit.
• Launch to all customers immediately, since…: Competitive pressure does not justify unmanaged risk to customers.

Key takeaway: Match launch caution to the impact on people.

stem: A project sponsor asks what the company's commitment to 'privacy by design' means for a new AI project. Which description is accurate?

choices.text: Building data protection into the system from the start, such as collecting only needed data
Encrypting the model's source code so competitors cannot copy the algorithm
Adding a privacy policy link to the company's website after the AI system has already launched to customers
Keeping all AI projects secret so that nobody outside the team knows they exist

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Privacy by design means considering data protection throughout design and development, including minimization and access controls.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Encrypting the model's source code so…: Protecting code is IP protection, not privacy.
• Adding a privacy policy link to the…: Adding a link after launch is not design.
• Keeping all AI projects secret so that…: Secrecy is not privacy protection.

Key takeaway: Build privacy into AI systems from the start.

stem: Which TWO signals should trigger a review of a deployed AI system? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The system's dashboard being moved to a different office monitor
The quarterly all-hands meeting being rescheduled to another date
A significant change in the population or data the system serves
A new team member joining the department that uses the system
A noticeable change in the system's accuracy or error patterns

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Changes in performance or in the data and population served are key signals that a system may no longer be safe or effective.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The system's dashboard being moved to a…: Display changes are irrelevant.
• The quarterly all-hands meeting being…: Meeting schedules are irrelevant.
• A new team member joining the department…: Staffing changes do not affect the system's behavior.

Key takeaway: Review AI when performance or the population it serves changes.

stem: A company's leaders want to know whether the organization can support an AI initiative. Which assessment area is most often overlooked?

choices.text: Whether the processes and people that must change to use the AI output are ready to change
Whether the office Wi-Fi is fast enough for employees to read project update emails
Whether the company's logo will look good on the AI project's internal status dashboard and reports
Whether the project team has enough desks in the same room for daily stand-up meetings

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AI only creates value when workflows and people adopt its outputs; organizational readiness is frequently underestimated compared with technology readiness.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Whether the office Wi-Fi is fast enough for…: Email Wi-Fi is not a readiness factor.
• Whether the company's logo will look good on…: Branding is irrelevant.
• Whether the project team has enough desks in…: Seating is a logistics detail.

Key takeaway: Assess process and people readiness, not just technology.

stem: An AI maturity assessment shows a company has strong data platforms but little experience deploying models to production. Which next step fits best?

choices.text: Buy additional data storage, since the assessment found data platforms to be the main gap
Start ten complex AI projects at once so teams gain experience as quickly as possible
Build MLOps practices through a small production deployment with monitoring and support
Stop all AI work until the company hires a large team that already has production experience

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The gap is production capability. A focused deployment that builds deployment, monitoring, and support practices addresses it directly.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Buy additional data storage, since the…: Data platforms are already strong.
• Start ten complex AI projects at once so…: Many complex projects at once overwhelm a team without production experience.
• Stop all AI work until the company hires a…: Waiting delays learning.

Key takeaway: Close the specific maturity gap the assessment finds.

stem: A company wants to use AI across departments, but each department stores customer data under different definitions of 'active customer.' Which foundational step helps most?

choices.text: Remove the 'active customer' field from all datasets so there is nothing to disagree on
Agree on shared business definitions and a data catalog that documents them
Let each department keep its own definition and have the AI decide which one to use
Build a separate model for each department's definition and compare results monthly

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Shared definitions, documented in a catalog, make data consistent across departments so AI outputs are comparable and trustworthy.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Remove the 'active customer' field from all…: Removing a key field loses information.
• Let each department keep its own definition…: AI cannot resolve business definitions on its own.
• Build a separate model for each department's…: Separate models multiply inconsistency.

Key takeaway: Align business definitions before scaling AI across departments.

stem: A company must choose between building a modern data platform first or starting an AI use case on existing messy data. Which approach usually works best?

choices.text: Build a complete enterprise data platform over several years before attempting any AI use case at all
Start many AI use cases on the messy data and accept whatever accuracy the models produce
Buy a new AI tool that promises to work perfectly without any data preparation at all
Start a focused use case while improving the data it needs, so platform work is guided by real needs

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Pairing a valuable use case with targeted data improvements delivers results sooner and prioritizes platform work that matters.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Build a complete enterprise data platform…: Long platform-first efforts delay value and may build the wrong things.
• Start many AI use cases on the messy data…: Ignoring data quality produces poor results.
• Buy a new AI tool that promises to work…: No tool removes the need for data preparation.

Key takeaway: Let valuable use cases drive incremental data foundation work.

stem: Middle managers are resisting an AI tool that changes how their teams work. What is the most effective leadership response?

choices.text: Delay the rollout until every manager voluntarily asks for the tool on their own
Bypass managers and communicate directly with their teams to speed up the rollout
Involve managers in designing the new workflows and define how their teams' success will be measured
Replace the managers who resist with new hires who are already enthusiastic about using AI tools at work

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Managers shape how teams work. Involving them in workflow design and success measures turns them into advocates.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Delay the rollout until every manager…: Waiting for voluntary requests stalls change.
• Bypass managers and communicate directly…: Bypassing managers increases resistance.
• Replace the managers who resist with new…: Replacement is disruptive and costly.

Key takeaway: Bring middle managers into the design of AI-enabled work.

stem: A company is creating an AI center of excellence. Which TWO responsibilities fit this group best? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Support business teams with expertise while those teams own their use cases
Approve all hiring decisions for the company, since hiring affects AI readiness
Replace the finance team's budgeting process with an AI-driven process immediately
Build and run every AI system in the company without involving business teams
Set shared standards, reusable components, and best practices for AI projects

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A center of excellence accelerates AI by providing standards, reusable assets, and expert support, while business teams stay accountable for outcomes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Approve all hiring decisions for the…: Hiring authority is outside its role.
• Replace the finance team's budgeting process…: Replacing finance processes is not its mandate.
• Build and run every AI system in the company…: Doing everything centrally creates a bottleneck and weak business ownership.

Key takeaway: A CoE enables and standardizes; business teams own outcomes.

stem: A pilot showed strong results with a highly motivated team. What is the main risk when scaling to the whole company?

choices.text: The model will become less accurate simply because many more employees are using it every day
Other teams may be less engaged or have different processes, so results may not repeat
Scaling always doubles the model's accuracy, which may surprise business users
The AI vendor will refuse to support more than one team using the same product

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Pilot teams are often enthusiastic and well supported. Broader rollout meets different contexts, so adoption and results must be managed and measured.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The model will become less accurate simply…: More users do not reduce model accuracy by themselves.
• Scaling always doubles the model's accuracy,…: Scaling does not change accuracy.
• The AI vendor will refuse to support more…: Vendors typically support scaling.

Key takeaway: Pilot results may not generalize; plan for different teams and contexts.

stem: A company scaled an AI assistant, and costs grew faster than usage because each team configured it differently. Which step best controls this?

choices.text: Stop tracking costs by team, since total spending is the only number that matters
Allow each team to keep customizing freely, since flexibility always reduces overall costs
Remove the assistant from teams with the highest costs without investigating the causes
Standardize configurations and shared components, and monitor cost per use across teams

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Standard configurations and shared components reduce duplication, and unit-cost monitoring highlights where spending is inefficient.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Stop tracking costs by team, since total…: Per-team visibility is needed to fix inefficiency.
• Allow each team to keep customizing freely,…: Unmanaged customization caused the problem.
• Remove the assistant from teams with the…: Removing without analysis may cut valuable use.

Key takeaway: Standardize and monitor unit costs when scaling AI.

stem: Which statement best describes technical readiness versus organizational readiness for AI?

choices.text: They are the same concept, measured twice by different departments for budgeting purposes
Technical readiness covers leadership support; organizational readiness covers GPU availability, storage, and networking
Only technical readiness matters, since organizations adapt automatically to new AI systems
Technical readiness covers data and infrastructure; organizational readiness covers skills, processes, and leadership

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Successful AI requires both the technical foundations and the organizational capacity to adopt and sustain it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• They are the same concept, measured twice by…: They cover different dimensions.
• Technical readiness covers leadership…: The definitions are swapped.
• Only technical readiness matters, since…: Organizations do not adapt automatically.

Key takeaway: AI readiness is both technical and organizational.

stem: A company needs to share data across teams for AI while restricting sensitive columns to authorized users. Which capability supports this?

choices.text: Keeping each team's data on separate laptops with no shared storage
Centralized, fine-grained data access controls on the shared data lake
Giving every employee full access so no team is blocked from using data
Emailing spreadsheet extracts to each team whenever they request data

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Fine-grained, centrally managed permissions enable sharing while protecting sensitive data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Keeping each team's data on separate laptops…: Laptop silos prevent sharing and are insecure.
• Giving every employee full access so no team…: Full access exposes sensitive data.
• Emailing spreadsheet extracts to each team…: Email extracts are uncontrolled copies.

Key takeaway: Share data for AI through governed, fine-grained access.

stem: Which communication approach best supports an AI transformation?

choices.text: Explain the purpose, expected changes to roles, and how employees will be supported, and repeat it regularly
Announce the transformation once in a company-wide email and avoid further discussion of it
Share only technical details about models so employees understand the underlying algorithms
Communicate only with executives until the transformation is complete to avoid distraction

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Clear, repeated communication about purpose, role changes, and support reduces uncertainty and builds trust.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Announce the transformation once in a…: One-time announcements leave questions unanswered.
• Share only technical details about models so…: Technical detail does not address people's concerns.
• Communicate only with executives until the…: Excluding employees breeds rumor and resistance.

Key takeaway: Communicate purpose, impact, and support clearly and repeatedly.

stem: Which TWO signals indicate an AI pilot is ready to scale? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A competitor has announced a similar AI initiative this month
The vendor offered a discount if the company expands this year
The operating model, support, and costs at scale are understood
The pilot team enjoyed the work and wants to continue it
It met its agreed success metrics against a baseline

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Scaling needs evidence of value and a realistic plan for operating at scale, including support and costs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A competitor has announced a similar AI…: Competitor moves do not prove readiness.
• The vendor offered a discount if the company…: Discounts do not show value or readiness.
• The pilot team enjoyed the work and wants to…: Team enthusiasm is not evidence of value.

Key takeaway: Scale when value is proven and operations at scale are planned.

stem: A legal team wants an assistant to summarize 400-page case files that exceed the model's context window. Which approach lets every section influence the summary?

choices.text: Ask the model to guess the contents of the missing pages based on the case title alone
Send only the first pages that fit in the context window and ignore the remaining pages
Increase the temperature so the model can process more pages in a single request
Summarize sections separately, then combine those summaries into a final summary

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Splitting long documents into sections and summarizing in stages (map-reduce or iterative refinement) lets all content contribute despite context limits.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Ask the model to guess the contents of the…: Guessing invents content.
• Send only the first pages that fit in the…: Ignoring pages loses information.
• Increase the temperature so the model can…: Temperature does not change the context window.

Key takeaway: Handle long documents by summarizing in stages.

stem: A leader asks what 'training' a model means in plain business terms. Which explanation is accurate?

choices.text: Writing the marketing message that explains the model's benefits to the company's customers and partners
Showing the model many examples so it adjusts itself to capture patterns useful for the task
Teaching employees how to use the model's user interface during an onboarding workshop
Installing the model on company servers and configuring its network security settings

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Training adjusts a model's internal parameters using example data so it learns patterns it can apply to new inputs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Writing the marketing message that explains…: That is marketing.
• Teaching employees how to use the model's…: That is user training.
• Installing the model on company servers and…: That is deployment.

Key takeaway: Training = learning patterns from example data.

stem: A telecom wants to predict network equipment failures from sensor readings and also generate plain-language repair notes for technicians. Which combination fits?

choices.text: A translation model for the sensor data and a speech model for the technicians' repair notes
A single image classification model that reads the sensor data and also writes the repair notes automatically
A predictive model on sensor data for failures, plus a generative model to draft the repair notes
A recommendation model for failures and a sentiment model to write repair notes for technicians

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Different tasks call for different AI types: predictive models for failure risk from sensor data, and generative models for readable notes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A translation model for the sensor data and…: Translation and speech do not predict failures.
• A single image classification model that…: Image classification does not fit sensor data or writing.
• A recommendation model for failures and a…: Recommendation and sentiment do not fit these tasks.

Key takeaway: Combine AI types when a solution has different kinds of tasks.

stem: A company's agent must look up inventory, check shipping rules, and then quote a delivery date. Which TWO elements are essential? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Defined tools or APIs the agent can call for inventory and shipping data
Removing all instructions so the agent can decide freely how it should respond
A larger image model to render product photos alongside each quote
A higher temperature so the agent chooses more creative delivery dates
Clear limits and logging for what the agent is allowed to do on its own

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Agents act through defined tools, and they need boundaries and logs so their actions are safe and reviewable.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Removing all instructions so the agent can…: Removing instructions reduces reliability.
• A larger image model to render product…: Images are unrelated to the task.
• A higher temperature so the agent chooses…: Creativity is inappropriate for delivery quotes.

Key takeaway: Agents need defined tools and clear boundaries.

stem: A company wants to present an AI business case to its board. Which element most strengthens credibility?

choices.text: A list of AI buzzwords that show the company understands current technology trends
Assumptions stated explicitly, with ranges for benefits and costs rather than single optimistic numbers
The highest possible benefit estimate, since boards respond best to large numbers
A promise that the project carries no risks at all, since any stated risk makes boards reluctant to invest

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Transparent assumptions and ranges show realistic thinking and let the board judge risk.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A list of AI buzzwords that show the company…: Buzzwords do not support a business case.
• The highest possible benefit estimate, since…: Optimistic single numbers undermine trust.
• A promise that the project carries no risks…: Claiming no risk is not credible.

Key takeaway: Credible business cases show assumptions and ranges.

stem: A company wants AI to support its sustainability goals. Which initiative aligns most directly?

choices.text: Generating more social media posts about sustainability each week
Creating AI artwork for the cover of the company's annual sustainability report
Translating the sustainability report into more languages for investors
Optimizing delivery routes to reduce fuel use and emissions per shipment

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Route optimization directly reduces fuel consumption and emissions, which advances the goal itself rather than communication about it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Generating more social media posts about…: Posts communicate but do not reduce impact.
• Creating AI artwork for the cover of the…: Artwork is cosmetic.
• Translating the sustainability report into…: Translation widens reach but does not reduce emissions.

Key takeaway: Align AI to initiatives that move the goal, not only communicate it.

stem: A company builds an AI feature on top of a partner's platform. Which TWO risks should the strategy address? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Dependence on the partner's roadmap, pricing, and availability
Whether the partner's executives attend the company's annual conference
Whether the partner's brand colors match the company's product design
Whether the partner's office is located in the same time zone as the company
Whether the company can move its data and prompts if the partnership ends

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Building on a partner creates dependency; the strategy should manage roadmap, pricing, and availability risk, and preserve portability.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Whether the partner's executives attend the…: Conference attendance is irrelevant.
• Whether the partner's brand colors match the…: Brand colors are cosmetic.
• Whether the partner's office is located in…: Time zone is a minor logistics issue.

Key takeaway: Manage partner dependency and preserve portability.

stem: An AI tool reduces the time to produce a quarterly report from ten days to three. What is the most meaningful way to express its value?

choices.text: The number of pages in the report, since shorter reports are always more valuable to executives
The number of AI models the tool uses internally, since more models indicate more business value
The business benefit of faster insights, such as earlier decisions, plus the staff time freed for other work
The time the IT team spent installing the tool, since installation effort reflects the tool's value

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Value comes from what faster reporting enables, such as timelier decisions, and from redeployed staff time.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The number of pages in the report, since…: Page count is not value.
• The number of AI models the tool uses…: Model count is not value.
• The time the IT team spent installing the…: Installation effort is a cost, not value.

Key takeaway: Express time savings in terms of what they enable.

stem: A retailer's AI pricing tool sets different prices for the same product in different neighborhoods. What responsible AI question should leaders ask?

choices.text: Whether the tool's vendor has won any retail industry awards in the last three years
Whether the pricing dashboard loads quickly on the store managers' tablets
Whether price differences disadvantage certain communities unfairly or unlawfully
Whether the tool updates prices fast enough to match competitors every hour

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Location-based pricing can disproportionately affect certain communities; fairness and legality must be assessed.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Whether the tool's vendor has won any retail…: Awards do not address fairness.
• Whether the pricing dashboard loads quickly…: Dashboard speed is technical.
• Whether the tool updates prices fast enough…: Speed is operational.

Key takeaway: Check whether AI-driven decisions disadvantage groups unfairly.

stem: A company's AI assistant will process data of EU residents. Which governance steps are most important before launch? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Assess whether the use case falls into a regulated risk category under EU AI rules
Avoid informing users about AI involvement to reduce support requests
Delay documentation until after launch to speed up delivery
Store all data in as many countries as possible for resilience, regardless of transfer rules
Confirm a lawful basis and data protection measures for processing personal data

explanation:
Why this is correct:
EU deployments must address data protection obligations and the risk classification rules that apply to AI systems.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Avoid informing users about AI involvement…: Hiding AI use conflicts with transparency obligations.
• Delay documentation until after launch to…: Documentation is needed before launch for many uses.
• Store all data in as many countries as…: Unrestricted transfers can breach data rules.

Key takeaway: Check data protection and AI risk classification before EU launches.

stem: A company fears its AI assistant might reveal internal documents to employees who should not see them. Which control addresses this?

choices.text: Remove all internal documents so the assistant can only answer general questions
Enforce the user's existing document permissions when the assistant retrieves content
Tell employees not to ask the assistant about any documents they are not allowed to read
Let the assistant decide on its own which employees seem trustworthy enough

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Retrieval should respect each user's access rights, so the assistant only uses content that user is allowed to see.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Remove all internal documents so the…: Removing documents removes the assistant's value.
• Tell employees not to ask the assistant…: Instructions do not enforce access.
• Let the assistant decide on its own which…: Model judgment is not access control.

Key takeaway: AI assistants must enforce existing access permissions.

stem: A company distinguishes 'explainability' from 'transparency' in its AI principles. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: Explainability describes where AI is used; transparency describes the math behind each individual prediction
Both terms mean encrypting the model so that its decisions cannot be manipulated by attackers
Both terms mean publishing the model's source code so that anyone can inspect the algorithm used
Explainability describes why a specific output was produced; transparency describes openness about how and where AI is used

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Explainability concerns reasons for individual outputs; transparency concerns disclosure about AI use, data, and limitations.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Explainability describes where AI is used;…: The definitions are swapped.
• Both terms mean encrypting the model so that…: Encryption is security, not explanation or disclosure.
• Both terms mean publishing the model's…: Publishing code is neither by itself.

Key takeaway: Explainability explains outputs; transparency discloses use.

stem: A company wants to measure whether its AI upskilling program is working. Which indicator is most meaningful?

choices.text: The number of certificates printed and displayed in office hallways
The number of employees who opened the training platform at least once this year
The total hours of training videos available in the course library
Employees applying AI to real tasks and improving related work outcomes

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Training succeeds when people apply skills to real work with measurable effect, not merely when content is available or opened.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The number of certificates printed and…: Certificates displayed are not outcomes.
• The number of employees who opened the…: Opening the platform is not learning.
• The total hours of training videos available…: Content volume is not impact.

Key takeaway: Measure upskilling by applied use and outcomes.

stem: A company is replacing a manual process with AI across all regions. Which transition approach reduces operational risk?

choices.text: Switch every region to AI on the same day and retire the manual process immediately
Keep the manual process running forever alongside the AI process in every region
Run the AI and manual processes in parallel briefly, compare results, then switch over region by region
Let each region decide independently whether to use AI without any comparison of results

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A short parallel run validates results, and a phased cutover limits the impact of any issue.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Switch every region to AI on the same day…: A big-bang switch maximizes risk.
• Keep the manual process running forever…: Permanent duplication wastes the benefit.
• Let each region decide independently whether…: No comparison leaves quality unknown.

Key takeaway: Validate with a parallel run and cut over in phases.

stem: A company's AI use cases need compute that scales up and down quickly, but finance wants predictable spending. Which approach balances both?

choices.text: Cap all AI workloads at a tiny fixed capacity so that costs never change from one month to the next
Use elastic cloud capacity with budgets, alerts, and commitments for the steady baseline
Buy fixed on-premises hardware sized for the highest possible peak demand forever
Use elastic capacity with no monitoring, since cloud bills are always predictable

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Elastic capacity meets variable demand, while budgets, alerts, and commitments for steady usage give finance predictability.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Cap all AI workloads at a tiny fixed…: Tiny fixed caps block value.
• Buy fixed on-premises hardware sized for the…: Peak-sized hardware sits idle and is costly.
• Use elastic capacity with no monitoring,…: Unmonitored cloud use can surprise finance.

Key takeaway: Pair elastic capacity with budgets and commitments.

stem: Which TWO findings in a readiness assessment most justify delaying an AI launch? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The data needed for the use case cannot legally be used for that purpose
The dashboard colors do not yet match the company's new brand guide
The planned launch date conflicts with a team member's approved vacation week
The project team would prefer a different name for the AI assistant
No one is accountable for monitoring the system after launch

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Missing post-launch ownership and unlawful data use are fundamental problems; the others are minor.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The dashboard colors do not yet match the…: Colors are cosmetic.
• The planned launch date conflicts with a…: Scheduling is easily solved.
• The project team would prefer a different…: Naming is cosmetic.

Key takeaway: Delay for accountability gaps and legal data issues, not cosmetics.

stem: A model that detects damaged parcels from photos performs well in daylight but poorly on night-shift photos. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Training images were mostly taken in daylight, so night conditions were underrepresented
Image models only work in daylight because they rely on sunlight to detect the parcel edges
Night-shift employees upload photos in a file format that models are unable to read at all
The model automatically switches off its accuracy features during the night shift hours

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Models perform best on conditions similar to their training data. Underrepresented conditions, such as low light, lead to poor performance.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Image models only work in daylight because…: Models can work at night if trained on such images.
• Night-shift employees upload photos in a…: File format is not the stated problem and is easily handled.
• The model automatically switches off its…: Models do not have time-based accuracy switches.

Key takeaway: Cover all real operating conditions in training data.

stem: A fraud team can lower the model's alert threshold to catch more fraud, but analysts can only review 500 alerts a day. How should the threshold be chosen?

choices.text: Choose the threshold at random each week so that fraudsters cannot predict the setting
Balance fraud caught against analyst capacity and the cost of each type of error
Always use the lowest threshold, since catching every possible fraud case is the only goal
Always use the highest threshold, since fewer alerts always means a better fraud program

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Thresholds trade recall against workload and false alarms. The right setting reflects business costs and operational capacity.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Choose the threshold at random each week so…: Random thresholds make performance unpredictable.
• Always use the lowest threshold, since…: Too many alerts overwhelm analysts and real fraud gets missed in the queue.
• Always use the highest threshold, since…: Too few alerts let fraud through.

Key takeaway: Set model thresholds by weighing error costs and operational capacity.

stem: Which description best distinguishes classification from regression?

choices.text: Classification predicts a number, such as next month's revenue; regression predicts a category label for each case
Classification requires no training data, while regression requires large labeled training datasets
Classification predicts a category, such as approve or decline; regression predicts a number, such as a price
Classification works only with images, while regression works only with text and tabular data

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Classification assigns categories; regression estimates continuous values.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Classification predicts a number, such as…: The definitions are reversed.
• Classification requires no training data,…: Both typically require labeled data.
• Classification works only with images, while…: Both work with many data types.

Key takeaway: Categories → classification; numbers → regression.

stem: A marketing team claims its model shows that customers who use the mobile app spend more, so pushing app downloads will raise spending. What is the key caution?

choices.text: The finding is invalid because spending data should never be combined with behavior data
Mobile app data cannot be used in models, so the finding must be discarded immediately
Models always prove causation, so the team should push app downloads to every customer as quickly as possible
The model shows correlation; high spenders may simply be more likely to use the app, not the reverse

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Predictive models find associations, not necessarily causes. Testing the intervention, for example with an experiment, shows whether pushing downloads changes spending.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The finding is invalid because spending data…: Combining these data types is common and useful.
• Mobile app data cannot be used in models, so…: App data can be used.
• Models always prove causation, so the team…: Predictive models do not prove causation.

Key takeaway: Correlation from a model is not proof that an intervention will work.

stem: A company wants to automatically route incoming customer emails to billing, technical, or sales teams. Which AI approach fits?

choices.text: Time-series forecasting that predicts next month's total email volume by team
Image generation that creates a visual summary of each incoming customer email
Speech synthesis that reads each email aloud to the team that receives it
Text classification that assigns each email to one of the three categories

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Assigning text to predefined categories is a text classification task, which services such as Amazon Comprehend support.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Time-series forecasting that predicts next…: Forecasting predicts volume, not routing.
• Image generation that creates a visual…: Images do not route emails.
• Speech synthesis that reads each email aloud…: Reading aloud does not categorize.

Key takeaway: Routing text to fixed categories is text classification.

stem: A retailer wants to know how many units of each product to stock next month in each store. Which type of AI problem is this, and which data matters most?

choices.text: Machine translation, using product descriptions written in several languages for each region
Demand forecasting, using historical sales by store and product plus known events such as promotions
Sentiment analysis, using customer reviews of products posted on the retailer's website over the last year
Image classification, using photos of store shelves taken by employees during the previous month

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Predicting future quantities over time is forecasting; it relies on sales history and known drivers of demand.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Machine translation, using product…: Translation is unrelated.
• Sentiment analysis, using customer reviews…: Sentiment is a weak signal for unit demand.
• Image classification, using photos of store…: Shelf photos do not forecast demand directly.

Key takeaway: Stock planning is a forecasting problem driven by history and known events.

stem: A small business wants to add AI-generated product descriptions to its online shop this week. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Use a managed foundation model through an API with a well-written prompt template
Hire a research team to train a custom language model from scratch over the next year
Build its own GPU cluster to host an open-source model before starting the project
Collect a million labeled product descriptions before writing any descriptions at all

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Managed foundation models accessed through APIs deliver results quickly without infrastructure or training.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Hire a research team to train a custom…: A custom model is far beyond the need and timeline.
• Build its own GPU cluster to host an…: Self-hosting adds cost and delay without benefit.
• Collect a million labeled product…: Labeled data is unnecessary for this generation task.

Key takeaway: For quick generative wins, use managed models through APIs.

stem: A team mentions a 'system prompt' in its assistant design. What is it?

choices.text: A pop-up message that asks users to update their web browser before using the assistant
The computer's operating system command line that engineers use to restart the server
Standing instructions that set the assistant's role, rules, and style for every conversation
The final answer the model gives at the end of each conversation with a customer

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A system prompt provides persistent instructions that shape the model's behavior across interactions.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A pop-up message that asks users to update…: Browser pop-ups are unrelated.
• The computer's operating system command line…: That is a shell, not a system prompt.
• The final answer the model gives at the end…: The answer is output, not a prompt.

Key takeaway: The system prompt sets role, rules, and style.

stem: A company's assistant answers well in testing but poorly on real customer questions, which are phrased very differently. Which approach best diagnoses the problem?

choices.text: Switch off logging so that poor real-world answers are not recorded anywhere
Rerun the original test set until the scores become even higher than before
Evaluate the assistant on a sample of real customer questions and compare errors with the test set
Assume customers are asking the wrong kinds of questions, and add a warning banner to the chat window

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A mismatch between test data and real inputs is a common cause of poor production quality. Evaluating on real questions reveals the gap to fix.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Switch off logging so that poor real-world…: Hiding evidence prevents improvement.
• Rerun the original test set until the scores…: Retesting on the same set hides the gap.
• Assume customers are asking the wrong kinds…: Blaming users does not fix the assistant.

Key takeaway: Evaluate AI on inputs that look like real usage.

stem: An assistant needs to answer questions about a product's 3,000-page technical manual. Which approach is most practical?

choices.text: Ask the model to answer from memory, since it probably read the manual during training
Index the manual for retrieval so relevant sections are provided to the model with each question
Summarize the manual into one paragraph and use only that paragraph for every question
Paste the entire manual into every prompt, regardless of which question a user asks or how short it is

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Retrieval provides only the relevant sections per question, which scales to large documents and keeps answers grounded.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Ask the model to answer from memory, since…: The model may never have seen the manual.
• Summarize the manual into one paragraph and…: One paragraph loses most details.
• Paste the entire manual into every prompt,…: The manual is too large and costly to send every time.

Key takeaway: Use retrieval for large reference documents.

stem: Which statement best compares a chatbot, an assistant grounded in company data, and an agent?

choices.text: A chatbot converses; a grounded assistant answers from company sources; an agent can also plan and take actions
All three are identical products that differ only in the price vendors charge for each of them
A chatbot can take actions, while an agent can only answer questions using general knowledge
A grounded assistant cannot use any company data, while a chatbot always uses internal documents

explanation:
Why this is correct:
These represent increasing capability: conversation, grounded answers from company data, and autonomous planning with actions through tools.

Why the other options are wrong:
• All three are identical products that differ…: They differ in capability, not only price.
• A chatbot can take actions, while an agent…: The roles are reversed.
• A grounded assistant cannot use any company…: Grounded assistants use company data by definition.

Key takeaway: Chatbot → grounded assistant → agent adds actions.

stem: Which TWO statements about AI model outputs should business users understand? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Outputs never change, even if the model is updated or retrained later
Outputs are always correct once a model passes its initial testing phase
Outputs are guaranteed to be unbiased if the model came from a large vendor
Outputs can be wrong even when the model is usually accurate
Outputs should be checked more carefully when decisions have high impact

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Models make errors and can change over time; the level of checking should match the stakes of the decision.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Outputs never change, even if the model is…: Updates can change outputs.
• Outputs are always correct once a model…: Passing tests does not guarantee correctness.
• Outputs are guaranteed to be unbiased if the…: Vendor size does not guarantee fairness.

Key takeaway: Treat AI outputs as fallible and check them in proportion to impact.

stem: A bank wants to extract key terms from thousands of commercial loan agreements and flag unusual clauses. Which TWO capabilities are most relevant? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Time-series forecasting to predict how many agreements arrive next year
Language models that identify and summarize clauses that differ from the standard
Speech synthesis to read each agreement aloud to the loan officers
Image generation to create illustrations of each loan agreement's terms
Document processing that extracts text and fields from the agreements

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Extracting content from documents and using language models to compare clauses against standards address both parts of the need.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Time-series forecasting to predict how many…: Volume forecasts do not analyze documents.
• Speech synthesis to read each agreement…: Audio does not extract terms.
• Image generation to create illustrations of…: Illustrations do not analyze clauses.

Key takeaway: Pair document extraction with language understanding for contract review.

stem: A data scientist says a model has 'high variance.' What does this mean for the business?

choices.text: The model produces many different languages, which makes it suitable for global rollouts
The model's predictions vary by region because each region has a separate licensing agreement with the vendor
The model is sensitive to the specific training data and may perform inconsistently on new cases
The model costs different amounts each month depending on the number of users logged in

explanation:
Why this is correct:
High variance means the model fits its training data too closely, so its performance on new data can be unstable, which is a form of overfitting.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The model produces many different languages,…: Language support is unrelated.
• The model's predictions vary by region…: Licensing does not create variance.
• The model costs different amounts each month…: Cost variation is unrelated.

Key takeaway: High variance = unstable performance on new data (overfitting risk).

stem: A company wants its assistant to answer in the same structure every time: summary, risks, next steps. What is the simplest effective approach?

choices.text: Provide a template in the prompt with an example of the desired structure
Ask users to reformat each answer themselves into the required three-part structure
Raise the temperature so the model tries different structures and learns the best one
Fine-tune a new model from scratch so it always uses the three-part structure

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A prompt template with an example is usually enough to produce a consistent structure, without training.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Ask users to reformat each answer themselves…: Pushing work to users defeats the purpose.
• Raise the temperature so the model tries…: Higher temperature reduces consistency.
• Fine-tune a new model from scratch so it…: Training from scratch is unnecessary.

Key takeaway: Use prompt templates and examples for consistent structure.

stem: A company's AI program has many small experiments but none reach production. Which strategic change helps most?

choices.text: Launch even more experiments so that at least one eventually succeeds by chance alone
Let the data science team choose projects purely based on which techniques interest them most
